headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; Authelia↔ms-swift interaction is undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift can read/write files and process stdin/stdout, while Authelia exposes API-facing outputs via OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad network egress. A shared workspace or copied output could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other, but no direct shared channel is documented, so I choose the higher plausible severity.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange text through a shared directory or stdout/stderr bridge, then prompt injection is possible.
IF ms-swift parses Authelia-generated content as instructions, then attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent's inputs and outputs.
Strip instructions from any text passed between agents.
Add a human review step before ms-swift acts on Authelia output.
Disable automatic ingestion of files produced by the other agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift explicitly touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets, and can read/write the filesystem; Authelia has broad network egress and handles OAuth/OIDC flows. A shared workspace could expose sensitive artifacts to the other agent, and ms-swift may upload file contents to external model services, so leakage is plausible in default-style deployments.
conditions: IF both agents mount the same workspace, then files touched by ms-swift can be exposed to Authelia-side processing.
IF ms-swift forwards logs, checkpoints, or datasets to external APIs, then sensitive content can leave the environment.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate filesystem namespace.
Remove secrets from shared directories before either agent runs.
Restrict ms-swift to non-sensitive sample data.
Review outbound destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/OIDC-facing APIs, while ms-swift can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write files. Even without modify_git_state, they can still contend over shared mutable resources such as files, configs, or tokens; uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same configuration directory, then one can overwrite the other's files.
IF both agents use the same OAuth or API credentials, then token or state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign disjoint write paths to each agent.
Use separate credentials per agent.
Serialize access to shared config files.
Disable package installation in ms-swift unless needed.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions and API responses that ms-swift may ingest through files or stdin/stdout. Because ms-swift is capable of acting on text and running shell commands, a bad Authelia output could cascade into incorrect downstream actions; there is no documented verification barrier, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF ms-swift consumes Authelia output without validation, then incorrect auth or policy text can propagate into later steps.
IF ms-swift is configured to trigger scripts from parsed text, then a mistaken upstream result can cause downstream actions.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Require schema-checked outputs from Authelia.
Log and diff all handoffs before execution.
Limit ms-swift to read-only analysis of Authelia output.
requires-engineering: add typed contracts for inter-agent messages.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service with network egress, while ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets. The profiles do not state residency, certifications, or retention mismatches, so only a limited compliance gap is evidenced; I do not cite both agents because this risk is primarily about ms-swift's handling of sensitive artifacts.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ms-swift's datasets, checkpoints, or logs, then retention and residency controls must be checked.
IF Authelia forwards identity data to external services, then cross-border processing rules may apply.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ms-swift training artifacts.
Review retention settings for logs and checkpoints.
Confirm outbound endpoints for Authelia.
Document data-class handling for both agents.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
